subject: food-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Steak and kidney pudding made with suet pastry is an example of:
questions.explain: Steak and kidney pudding is a traditional British dish, reflecting British culinary heritage.

questions.q: Marketing techniques such as bright packaging and 'buy one get one free' offers mainly aim to:
options: Encourage consumers to buy the product
questions.explain: Marketing and special offers are designed to influence and encourage consumers to buy products.

questions.q: Which religious group commonly avoids beef because the cow is considered sacred?
questions.explain: Many Hindus avoid beef as the cow is regarded as sacred; many also follow a vegetarian diet.

questions.q: Food prepared according to Jewish dietary law is described as:
questions.explain: Kosher food follows Jewish dietary laws, which forbid pork and the mixing of meat and dairy.

questions.q: Which of the following must, by UK law, always be declared as one of the named allergens on packaged food?
questions.explain: Celery is one of the 14 allergens that must be emphasised on UK food labels; salt, onion and pepper are not on that list.

questions.q: Which sensory test is used to find whether tasters can detect a difference between samples?
questions.explain: A triangle test asks tasters to identify the odd sample, detecting whether a difference can be perceived.

questions.q: A person with a severe peanut allergy may suffer which life-threatening reaction?
questions.explain: A severe allergic reaction can cause anaphylaxis, a rapid, life-threatening response needing urgent treatment.

questions.q: Which group of consumers would a manufacturer most need to consider when developing a gluten-free product?
questions.explain: People with coeliac disease must avoid gluten, so gluten-free products are developed for them.

questions.q: Sensory evaluation of food involves testing its:
questions.explain: Sensory evaluation judges food using the senses: appearance, aroma, taste, texture and sometimes sound.

questions.q: A lacto-ovo vegetarian will eat:
options: Dairy and eggs but no meat or fish
questions.explain: A lacto-ovo vegetarian eats dairy and eggs but avoids meat, poultry and fish.

questions.q: A 'star profile' (sensory profiling) chart is mainly used to:
options: Record and compare different sensory characteristics of a food
questions.explain: A star/profile chart plots characteristics such as flavour, texture and appearance to compare foods.

questions.q: A Hindu following religious dietary rules is most likely to avoid:
questions.explain: Many Hindus avoid beef because the cow is regarded as sacred.

questions.q: The 'umami' taste detected during sensory evaluation is best described as:
questions.explain: Umami is the savoury, meaty taste found in foods such as cheese, mushrooms and meat.

questions.q: A person following a vegan diet will avoid:
options: All foods of animal origin, including dairy and eggs
questions.explain: Vegans avoid all animal products, including meat, fish, dairy, eggs and honey.

questions.q: By UK law, which of the following must always be clearly emphasised on food labels?
questions.explain: Food labels must clearly highlight any of the 14 major allergens (such as nuts, milk, eggs) present.

questions.q: A person with coeliac disease must avoid foods containing:
questions.explain: Coeliac disease is an autoimmune reaction to gluten, found in wheat, barley and rye, so it must be avoided.

questions.q: Which of these is a lifestyle factor that can affect a person's food choices?
options: Having little time to cook due to a busy job
The day of the week only
questions.explain: Lifestyle factors such as a busy job and limited time strongly influence the foods people choose.

questions.q: For someone on a low budget, which factor is most likely to influence their food choice?
questions.explain: Cost is a major factor for people on a limited budget when choosing what food to buy.

questions.q: Food that is prepared according to Islamic law and permitted for Muslims to eat is described as:
questions.explain: Halal means permitted under Islamic law; pork and alcohol are forbidden (haram).

questions.q: Lactose intolerance is the inability to properly digest the sugar found in:
questions.explain: Lactose is the natural sugar in milk and dairy, which people with lactose intolerance cannot digest well.

questions.q: In the traffic-light labelling system, a red label for a nutrient indicates the food is:
questions.explain: Red on a traffic-light label means the food is high in that nutrient (such as fat, sugar or salt).

questions.q: Under Jewish (kosher) dietary law, meat must not be eaten in the same meal as:
questions.explain: Jewish dietary law forbids mixing meat and dairy in the same meal.
